Recent findings suggest that in the desert, water doesn't arrive steadily. It comes in short pulses: a winter storm, a few rainy days, then months of drought. A desert plant needs two skills to live there. It has to survive the long dry spells, and it has to make full use of the brief windows when water is plentiful. A latest study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and the Volcani Institute shows that the prickly pear cactus has an unexpected way of doing both.

Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

📅 16 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 3 min read (648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere.
  • Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.
  • To start with, today’s patch finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s patch finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

In a recent development, the good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

In a recent development, patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark claims this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

According to recent reports, as for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

In a recent development, and, of course, it wouldn’t be a substantial Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

Sources indicate that the Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

📅 18 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (393 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated.
  • We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series.
  • It has been revealed that cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

It has been revealed that cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Industry observers note that software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

It has been revealed that however, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

It has been revealed that separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

It has been revealed that spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a substantial impact.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

Cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

In a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

In a recent development, professor Sahakian stated: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop important cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Sources indicate that despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Sources indicate that even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something new.

According to recent reports, one of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several notable areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

It has been revealed that early readers also demonstrated stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Dr. Langley said: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The important thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

The academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

The benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

In a recent development, for many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

According to recent reports, books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents said they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

In a recent development, as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

One study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

Another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

These findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

Industry observers note that what could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas vital for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

In one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

Following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in notable regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

According to recent reports, reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

The Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Rolled out on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

Sources indicate that it has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

Professor Sahakian remarked: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 has a wide variety of encounters that can crop up across its central locales. While most are tied to a specific area or mission, some of the game’s most memorable are those that can occur anywhere within a given zone, adding tons of random madness to Leonida while free-roaming.

In a recent development, many of these quests are direct references to other pieces of crime fiction, from subtle hints to straight-up placing the protagonists in the situation from the films. One such quest sees either Jason or Lucia held at gunpoint by a stand-in for Tom Cruise’s character from Collateral. If you want to trigger this event and get out alive, make sure to read on!

Recent findings suggest that this encounter is a standout, not appearing anywhere on the map and not being accessible until midway into Chapter 3. Once you’ve gained easy access to Vice City and start heading toward Vice Beach, sitting in any car alone for an extended period gives a suited stranger a chance to enter the back seat suddenly.

According to recent reports, he’ll proceed to stick up the protagonist, forcing them to start driving. From here on, failure to comply with his orders will lead to him shooting the player, not enough to kill outright, but enough to push you over the edge if you’re already wounded.

According to recent reports, your next task is to run a red light, any red light you can find. Thankfully, the agent is rather patient as long as he can tell you’re looking for a light or waiting for one to change. Once it’s clear you can follow instructions, he’ll mark an area near the park in Vice Beach for you to drive to, a trek depending on where you started the mission.

It has been revealed that make sure you don’t slow down too much or try to turn on the radio. Your passenger wants a nice, quiet ride to his destination. Once you arrive, things change fast, giving you a split-second decision.

Sources indicate that once you arrive at the location, the agent will explain that this entire charade was to put the protagonist’s face and car on a police suspect database for running that red light. Now that you’ve made it to his destination, we’re about to be in real hot water, as he guns down a nearby guard protecting a small drug lab.

Recent findings suggest that he insists you leave, but if you’re feeling spiteful or profit-focused, you can easily follow him inside. Without a gun to your head, he’s as easy to take down as any other enemy, plus he’ll have already cleared the guards inside and outside the lab.

Industry observers note that make sure to keep your car running by double-tapping your exit button, and swiftly pocket everything he stood to gain before heading out. He wasn’t kidding, the cops are already on their way, so whether you’re willing to snag some for yourself or just want to hightail it, make sure you leave fast.

Recent findings suggest that I’d fully recommend hitting the lab, as it’s easily a 10k payout for very little effort. There are also a few handy guns to pocket if you need the hardware. The Jeep parked outside sells for a pretty penny as well, giving you an excuse to swing by Randy and continue his questline.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the debut of the redesigned Mercedes-Benz GLA, firm chairman Ola Källenius mentioned, “The ICE [internal-combustion engine] world and the BEV [battery-electric vehicle] world have come together.” And that’s true: Apart from their grilles, the gas-engine GLA and the first-ever GLA EV are virtually indistinguishable from each other. Källenius described the design of the upcoming GLA as “clearly electric-first,” so it’s perhaps appropriate that the EV version is the first one we’re driving.

Electric-first is also the go-to-market strategy—at least in Europe. It was to be in the U.S., too, but there’s been a reversal; we’re now slated to get the GLA hybrid first. Really, though, we won’t be getting either one for a while. We’re told to expect the gas-engine GLA sometime late next year, while the EV won’t arrive until the first half of 2028. Our recent drive of the electric GLA in Spain, therefore, was an extra-long-lead preview.

See all results for newly introduced 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class EV for sale near 28217.

In a recent development, we’d say that gives buyers plenty of time to warm up to the upcoming styling, except that the look is not all that different from the current GLA. More substantial, maybe: The body is bigger, sitting astride a wheelbase that is stretched 2.4 inches. The new GLA is also longer, lower, and wider.

The GLA EV is also adorned with more three-pointed stars, though not to the extent of some other recent Mercedes products. Besides the illuminated logo on the flat-panel “grille,” there’s a large badge on the rear liftgate, and the motif also appears in the headlights and taillights. Opt for Sky Control for the standard glass roof panel, and 172 light-up stars appear on the glass, which is electronically dimmable in sections.

It has been revealed that the dash is lifted straight from the GLA’s sedan sibling, the CLA. As in other Benz models, there’s an available Superscreen that adds a 14.0-inch passenger display to the standard 14.0-inch center touchscreen and 10.3-inch instrument screen. With it, virtually the entire dashboard is given over to digital real estate. Sadly, almost none of the space contains any physical switchgear, although at least we still get air vents that can be aimed by hand. Wireless smartphone mirroring is standard, but a wireless charging pad costs extra. The navigation uses Google Maps and optionally offers Benz’s augmented reality, an inset showing a forward-camera view with overlaid arrows indicating direction. Unfortunately, that inset appears on the left side of the touchscreen, where it’s obscured by the driver’s right hand on the wheel; you have to peer around to see it.

In a recent development, the on-screen climate controls are another ergonomic fail, as the touch points to change the temperature are tiny, and you have to open the climate menu to adjust the fan speed. You could ask for help from Benz’s digital assistant, which lurks within the screen, always listening. And there’s a camera trained on the driver, which can use facial recognition to automatically call up the driver’s profile and saved preferences. It can also take selfies! In a more worthwhile use of technology, buyers can purchase dash-cam functionality for the forward-facing camera.

See all results for new 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class EV for sale near 28217.

Beyond the digital, the interior features high-back front seats that are firmly padded and well shaped. The high center console makes for a somewhat confining feel up front, but its floating design creates a large open bay underneath for storage. The rear-seat area boasts a flat floor and is much roomier than in the CLA sedan. The cargo hold is 15 cubic feet, expandable to 49 cubes with the rear seatbacks folded. There’s also a frunk that’s about the size of a carry-on suitcase.

It has been revealed that the powertrains mirror the CLA EV’s. There’s a single-motor GLA250+ that sends 268 horsepower to the rear wheels. The dual-motor GLA350 4Matic has all-wheel drive and 349 horses. Both employ a two-speed transmission on the rear axle for improved efficiency at highway speeds.

In a recent development, the standard suspension has passive dampers, but the cars we drove had the optional adaptive dampers and rode on 20-inch wheels (18s are standard; 19s are also available). The smooth pavement of Barcelona and sunny coastal environs gave the dampers little to adapt to—any real assessment of the GLA’s ride quality will have to wait until we drive one on the meaner streets back home. However, the suspension acquitted itself well on our drive route’s long series of hillside curves. The GLA is composed but would be more confidence-inspiring if the steering weren’t so light and remote.

The GLA isn’t a hot hatch, though; it’s more of an urban runabout. In that context, the 268-hp GLA250+ is adequately peppy, even though Mercedes posits a rather languid 60-mph time of 7.2 seconds. We expect it to do better than that, as the CLA250+ we tested managed a 5.8-second result. The dual-motor GLA350 felt much more energetic, particularly outside of urban environs, where it promptly passed dawdlers on two-lane roads and merged easily onto the freeway. For the GLA350, Mercedes claims a 5.3-second 60-mph time, but again that’s likely an undersell; testing a mechanically identical CLA350, we got 4.3 seconds. Even so, there are quicker EVs in this class, but one positive here is that even the higher-horsepower dual-motor version doesn’t feel like its output overwhelms its chassis—often an problem with high-horsepower EVs. Besides the standard drive modes of Eco, Comfort, Sport, and Individual, the dual-motor GLA adds a Terrain mode that optimizes the powertrain for loose surfaces; its camera system is able to stitch together a “transparent hood” view of what’s immediately in front of the car.

Industry observers note that when it comes time for slowing, there are three levels of liftoff regen (D, D+, and D-), as well as an Auto setting that varies the regen level based on info from the navigation system and the forward-facing cameras. Our preference is D-, which is essentially coasting, but D+ will please fans of one-pedal driving. We also tried the automated parking function, which was able to back into and out of a parallel-parking spot without trying our patience. It’s a digital add-on that’s purchased for a set time period; the same goes for the MBUX Entertainment package of multimedia streaming and app downloads.

Like the CLA EV sedan, the GLA is built on Benz’s MMA platform, with an 800-volt architecture and an 85-kWh battery. That architecture allows for speedy DC recharging, up to 320 kilowatts. Should you find a power source robust enough to reach that figure, Mercedes says the GLA battery can go from 10 percent to 80 percent in 22 minutes. (In our testing of the CLA250+ with the same hardware, it went from 10 to 80 percent in just 21 minutes.) EPA range estimates for the GLA aren’t yet available, but the CLA offers a clue, and its impressive range figures run from 312 miles on the low end to as high as 374 miles.

Sources indicate that if the GLA ends up with numbers like those, it’ll look pretty good against the electric Mini Countryman, Genesis GV60, and Cadillac Optiq, and similar-ish to a Rivian R2. Those look to be the GLA EV’s prime competitors at a base-price guesstimate of around $50K. But the EV landscape could shift significantly by the time the GLA gets here. After all, a lot can happen between now and 2028.

Breaking: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that light can carry vast amounts of information, but developing faster and more efficient optical communication systems requires precise control over how it travels.
  • According to recent reports, A research team led by KAIST has uncovered detailed information about how light moves through BTO and how much of it the material absorbs.
  • KAIST (President Choongsik Bae) confirmed the results on November 8.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that light can carry vast amounts of information, but developing faster and more efficient optical communication systems requires precise control over how it travels. Scientists have now made an important advance in understanding barium titanate (BTO), a promising material that could help improve the performance of future devices that transmit information using light.

According to recent reports, A research team led by KAIST has uncovered detailed information about how light moves through BTO and how much of it the material absorbs. These properties have been difficult to measure accurately for decades because of the crystal's complicated internal structure. The new findings provide engineers with a more reliable foundation for designing optical devices that minimize signal loss and support faster data transmission.

KAIST (President Choongsik Bae) confirmed the results on November 8. The research was led by Professor Min Seok Jang of KAIST's School of Electrical Engineering, working with Professor Harry A. Atwater's group at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS), and U.S.-based J.A. Woollam Co. Together, the researchers examined how BTO interacts with light across wavelengths extending from the ultraviolet to the far-infrared.

Why Barium Titanate Could Transform Optical Communications.

One of BTO's most valuable characteristics is its ability to change how it affects light when electricity is applied. This behavior, called the Pockels effect, gives the material a strong electro-optic response and makes it especially attractive for optical modulators. These components convert electrical information into signals carried by light, making them crucial building blocks for advanced communication systems.

However, producing reliable devices requires a detailed understanding of two fundamental optical properties. The refractive index describes how light travels through a material, while the extinction coefficient indicates how strongly the material absorbs it. Engineers need both measurements to predict how light will behave inside a waveguide, a structure designed to direct light along a specific path, and how much of the optical signal may be lost.

Getting consistent measurements from BTO has been surprisingly challenging. The material can contain multiple microscopic regions, called domains, in which the crystal structure points in different directions. Because these regions interact with light differently, measurements of an entire sample can combine several distinct responses. This has contributed to widely conflicting reports of BTO's optical properties over many decades.

Solving a Decades-Old Mystery About Light.

In a recent development, to overcome this problem, the researchers used a sophisticated measurement method known as Mueller matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry. The technique examines how the polarization of light changes when light reflects from or passes through a material, allowing scientists to investigate its optical behavior in detail.

Recent findings suggest that rather than relying on crystals containing a complicated mixture of differently oriented regions, the team studied two types of single-crystal samples with relatively consistent domain orientations. This approach helped minimize overlapping optical responses and allowed the researchers to identify the material's underlying properties more accurately.

Industry observers note that their measurements spanned wavelengths from 190 nanometers (nm) to 40 micrometers (μm), covering an exceptionally broad range of light from ultraviolet to far-infrared. Since a material's optical behavior changes with wavelength, the scientists divided the spectrum into three regions and applied a different analytical approach to each. This revealed how BTO's refractive index and light absorption depend on both wavelength and crystal orientation.

It has been revealed that the researchers also investigated a particularly notable range in which BTO allows nearly all incoming light to pass through. By combining ellipsometry with separate measurements of light transmission, they detected extremely low absorption, determining extinction coefficients of approximately 10-5 in the 2-10 μm wavelength range. These precise values will help engineers estimate how much light is lost as it travels through or remains confined within optical components.

It has been revealed that in another advance, the team developed a way to predict the combined optical behavior of crystals containing multiple domains. Their method uses the orientations of those domains and the proportion of the crystal occupied by each to calculate the material's overall response to light.

Opening the Door to Faster Data Transmission and Quantum Technology.

The results could make the development of future optical devices more predictable and efficient. With accurate information about BTO's behavior, engineers can model how light will travel through components of different shapes and dimensions before manufacturing them. They can also better estimate absorption losses, potentially reducing the need for repeated prototypes, costly redesigns, and extensive testing.

The potential benefits extend beyond conventional optical communications. BTO could also play an notable role in devices that produce light at different wavelengths, as well as photonic circuits that use light to process quantum information. Such technologies depend on controlling light with exceptional precision.

"This study reveals the optical response of barium titanate, which had long remained unclear, and provides a reliable reference for how the material interacts with light," said Professor Min Seok Jang.

Jang also emphasized that the findings could contribute to optical communication devices capable of transmitting data faster while reducing light loss. The improved understanding of BTO may also support the development of quantum photonic technologies, where precise manipulation of light is essential.

The study was published online on October 20, 2026, in ACS Photonics. Jiwon Kang, a Ph.D. candidate in KAIST's School of Electrical Engineering, and Dr. Nina Hong of J.A. Woollam Co. served as co-first authors. Professors Min Seok Jang of KAIST and Harry A. Atwater of Caltech were the corresponding authors.

Sources indicate that funding was provided through the Culture, Sports and Tourism R&D Program administered by the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA), with support from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; the Basic Science Research Program administered by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF), with support from the Ministry of Education; the Ministry of Science and ICT; and the U.S. Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports has revealed 3 upcoming Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

Industry observers note that the Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

Upcoming Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

It has been revealed that interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

If you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

Sources indicate that we’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

According to recent reports, europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Recent findings suggest that spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

Industry observers note that china will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

In a recent development, riot has not yet remarked how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

It has been revealed that worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

Recent findings suggest that the arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

According to recent reports, the city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

10 Best Food Centric Video Games

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For many countries across the globe, 2026’s holiday season is just around the corner.
  • While some people may be stressing out about the prospect of cooking so many dishes for the holiday season, there’s likely just as many people out there who not only enjoy tasting all kinds of meals but enjoy preparing them for friends and family alike as well.
  • For those who love cooking and all things food-related, here’s a look at the 10 best food centric video games people can enjoy playing through, whether solo or with friends, in between tantalizing holiday meals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For many countries across the globe, 2026’s holiday season is just around the corner. With those holidays come celebratory family gatherings full of all kinds of delicious food to eat.

While some people may be stressing out about the prospect of cooking so many dishes for the holiday season, there’s likely just as many people out there who not only enjoy tasting all kinds of meals but enjoy preparing them for friends and family alike as well.

For those who love cooking and all things food-related, here’s a look at the 10 best food centric video games people can enjoy playing through, whether solo or with friends, in between tantalizing holiday meals.

It has been revealed that for a few decades now, food companies have occasionally released tie-in video games often referred to as advergames, in wacky attempts to attract gamers to purchase their products. While Burger King has released a few advergames over the years, its best was arguably Sneak King.

One of three BK games for the original Xbox and Xbox 360, Sneak King is a third-person stealth game following the fast-food chain’s now-retired Burger King mascot, as he sneaks around various locations to surprise deliver BK meals such as omelet sandwiches, hash browns, and more.

While Sneak King didn’t have a lot of depth to it, the game did represent the often wacky yet creative game design the sixth and seventh console generations are remembered for.

Anybody who grew up owning an iPod Touch, iPad, or iPhone in the early 2010s likely played some of the most iconic mobile apps of all time, such as Angry Birds, Doodle Jump, and the subject for this entry, Halfbrick Studios’ Fruit Ninja.

The premise for Fruit Ninja is simple: players must use a touch screen, VR controllers, or their own hands (in the case of the Kinect versions) to equip ninja blades and slice up as much flying fruit as possible without hitting flying bombs.

Fruit Ninja is an easy game for sure, but it’s one that endlessly fun no matter what form or mode it’s played in, whether it be the Xbox 360 Kinect version, the Fruit Ninja FX version found at Dave & Buster's and other arcades, or the latest version on Nex Playground.

It has been revealed that J. R. R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings franchise is beloved for many reasons, such as its mythology, character arcs, and fantastical creatures. Another aspect of the franchise many people adore is the calm, joyful culture of Hobbit life.

Numerous LOTR fans strive to live life as merrily as the Shire’s inhabitants, and one way people can do so is by playing the life simulation game Tales of the Shire: A The Lord of the Rings Game, set after The Hobbit but before The Fellowship of the Ring.

Recent findings suggest that here, players can create their own Hobbit as they complete tasks such as farming, fishing, and decorating Hobbit-holes in the emerging Hobbiton village of Bywater. Most importantly for this article, they can also cook a variety of dishes for their Hobbit neighbors.

In 2006, Nintendo helped many young gamers get interested in cooking for the first time by releasing the minigame compilation Cooking Mama on the Nintendo DS. While that game is fantastic, many Nintendo players would consider Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! to be the best entry in the CM series.

Recent findings suggest that the final mainline entry in the CM series, Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! Features similar modes and overall gameplay to its predecessors, but introduces many latest minigames and recipes such as Pumpkin Gratin, Hawaiian Pancakes, and Herb Hotdogs.

Players could even manage a burger shop, take care of pet fish, customize kitchen designs, and gather ingredients from plants, with each action feeling more precise thanks to the 3DS’ improved stylus controls.

In a recent development, video games have let people play as medieval heroes, monsters, space marines, and more, but one unique game did the impossible by making playing as actual food fun. That game was Bossa Studios’ I Am Bread.

Set in the same universe as Surgeon Simulator, I Am Bread has players control a singular piece of bread as it strives to move about various locations such as a kitchen and a bathroom in an effort to become toast, whilst struggling to maintain its edibility by avoiding the ground, bugs, and other contaminants.

While the premise of I Am Bread might sound ridiculous at first, it actually winds up being a fairly hilarious, challenging, and rewarding game, with all of the crazy antics and chaos the slices of bread get into.

It has been revealed that people love parties, candy, and piñatas, but only one game developer has dared tackling the question of how piñatas are made. As seen in Rare’s classic life simulation game Viva Piñata.

Set on the initially ruinous Pinata island, Viva Piñata has players restore a garden on the island with the goal of attracting, domesticating, breeding, and defending local piñata wildlife, so that they can eventually be sent out to parties across the globe full of delicious candy.

Viva Piñata may be 20 years old at this point, but it’s still just as fun and colorful as ever, whether people play it on Xbox 360, PC, or via the Rare Replay compilation.

According to recent reports, the Illinois-based game developer Young Horses is famous for its Octodad series, which itself could be considered a food centric game since a chef chases Octodad around. However, the team wound up making one of the most creative food centric games yet in 2020, with Bugsnax.

Here, people play as a muppet-like Grumpus newspaper journalist, as they set out to Snaktooth Island to document the food-like Bugsnax creatures living there only to get caught up in a mysterious conspiracy surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

For anyone who wanted to explore the living food island of Swallow Falls in Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2, Bugsnax is the game for you. You can encounter all kinds of food-inspired wildlife on Snaktooth Island, such as the elephant cheeseburger Bunger and the crab apple Crapple.

Recent findings suggest that many of the best food centric games were released years or even decades ago, but one latest 2026 title has quickly become a favorite among food fanatics. That game being the anime-inspired cooking and restaurant management simulator KuloNiku: Bowl Up!

Recent findings suggest that the 13th game released by Gambir Studio, KuloNiku: Bowl Up! has players inherit their grandmother’s once-famous meatball restaurant in the cozy town of KuloNiku. They set out to restore it to its former glory by experimenting with latest recipes, decor, and competing with other chefs in Meatball Brawls.

People aren’t just making simple spaghetti and meatball dishes, though, as customers will often request comedically complex recipes requiring players to chop, boil, fry, and torch all kinds of ingredients, with some customers even going on to become potential friends or rivals.

Many food centric games focus on people opening up a newly introduced restaurant and rising to Michelin star status, but no game quite replicates that experience in such a unique and fun way like Mintrocket’s Dave the Diver.

A primarily 2D adventure and management game, Dave the Diver follows the title character as he and his friends open their Bancho Sushi Bar near a massive, mysterious Blue Hole, with Dave having to dive for fish during the day and manage the sushi restaurant at night.

Diving for fish and managing the sushi restaurant are certainly fun activities, but there's far more to Dave the Diver than initially meets the eye. Players can fight huge sea creature bosses, sing karaoke, and even interact with mermaids from the Sea People Village.

Without a doubt, the best food centric game out there is Ghost Town Games’ Overcooked! All You Can Eat, a remastered collection of Overcooked and Overcooked 2 with all DLC expansions and completely brand-fresh content.

A third-person, top-down perspective cooking game, Overcooked 1 and 2 feature teams of up to four chefs working together to serve food in an orderly, oftentimes hectic, manner from restaurants, food trucks, and unconventional locations such as a space station and icebergs.

While Overcooked may not be as realistic with its food as other games, it perfectly recreates the fun, often chaotic nature of restaurant cooking into a cartoony, co-op experience and forces people to learn to work together as a team, making it a perfect food centric game.

#155221. Tech Report: Zelda Ocarina Remake Producers Talk Changing And Maintaining The Game, Easter Eggs, The Bombchu Bowling Alley Operator, And More

📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3824 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Zelda Ocarina Remake Producers Talk Changing And Maintaining The Game, Easter Eggs, The Bombchu Bowling Alley Operator, And More

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today marks the release of the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2.
  • Topics include how the team approached remaking Ocarina of Time, what needed changing and what needed to stay the same, their thoughts on the Easter Eggs from the original game, the fate and marital status of the Bombchu Bowling girl, and more.
  • The discussion covers a fairly faithful remake of Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, which launched nearly 30 years ago, but I have spoiler-marked certain questions and answers that might be considered sensitive if you want to maintain surprise when playing the remake yourself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today marks the release of the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2. You can read my full, positive review here. Ahead of the game’s release, but after having played the game to completion (well… 99% as you will learn below), I traveled to Latest York to speak with Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma (whose work on the original Ocarina of Time marked his first involvement with the series) and Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi (director of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom among other Zelda titles).

Topics include how the team approached remaking Ocarina of Time, what needed changing and what needed to stay the same, their thoughts on the Easter Eggs from the original game, the fate and marital status of the Bombchu Bowling girl, and more.

The discussion covers a fairly faithful remake of Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, which launched nearly 30 years ago, but I have spoiler-marked certain questions and answers that might be considered sensitive if you want to maintain surprise when playing the remake yourself.

Mr. Fujibayashi, what is your relationship to Ocarina of Time?

Industry observers note that fujibayashi: Regarding the original Ocarina of Time, at the time I was working for a different company, so it was mainly me as an end user trying to looking forward to the experience of what a 3D Zelda is going to look like. So, really, I was just waiting in anticipation for that.

How long has the remake been in development?

In a recent development, aonuma: It's actually kind of hard to say exactly when development began because the earliest thought process was us thinking about the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda approaching, and so we started to have this conversation, “Oh, what should we make to mark this occasion?” And then at that point, we decided on Ocarina of Time, and so a lot of time elapsed from the beginning of that conversation about the anniversary until we got to Ocarina. So it's hard to pinpoint exactly when the development itself began.

Was this a more relaxing game to develop after making Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom back-to-back?

Industry observers note that aonuma: Was it relaxing? That's kind of a hard question to ask. I would say it's more a different style of development. So, if we looked at Tears of the Kingdom, Breath of the Wild, these were created as new games with a very different kind of development cycle. Whereas for a remake like this one, we decided to take an interesting approach, which is to bring in this new younger staff and find out what they would bring to this project in terms of their own experience, their own interpretation as newer staff.

And so my role here was really advising them on this, and it's not always like the development cycle of a fresh game. But in one sense, the producer has to be careful not to advise too much, to say that you must do it like this. You don't want to prescribe the approach that anyone is going to take. You want to make sure that there's enough space for these younger staff members to have their own interpretation, their own approach to it.

Do you have remake philosophies or rules, like what needs to stay the same and what should change?

Fujibayashi: So, in fact, there were pretty clear kind of rules or guidelines, as you stated. First, is because you know, as Mr. Aonuma had mentioned, where he wanted to, the development team was centered around the young directors that took part in this development. And when we first started discussing what kind of game and what kind of approach you wanted to take. One thing that really came through and we clarified was, as you mentioned, what are we going to change and what are we going to keep the same.

According to recent reports, and I'll start with what we wanted to change, and that was really to make sure that – because we have the ability to use the latest technology through the Nintendo Switch 2 – there's a lot we can change and improve upon, such as you know obviously things like controls, graphics. We also have a fresh controller, so that allows for the new camera controls. And we’re really able to fine tune and polish the feel of the game and there was excitement for all the ways of expression we can provide the player.

Sources indicate that but on the other hand, thinking about what we didn't want to change, we were thinking about the creators of the original Ocarina of Time, and what they wanted to convey, the experience that they wanted to provide for users and players through this title. That's something that we wanted to keep intact and that spirit to carry across. And we wanted to make sure that this new game is able to deliver that in the way that we wanted them to.

It has been revealed that aonuma: So speaking as someone who worked on the original Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, you always have those moments looking back of, “Oh, you know, I really wanted to do more of this,” or, “I wanted to be able to express this in a different way,” but you're faced with certainly the tech limitations of the time. And I went on from Ocarina of Time to work on other Zelda franchise titles, as well. And with each new title, you're always looking for a new way to express something that may not have been available to you previously. But you always have to keep in mind is what makes a Zelda game special, and how do we protect that? How do we keep that in store for the players, as well. So, on this project in particular, I had to think of that through the lens of how do we protect the things that make it the Zelda Ocarina experience, but also how do I give the freedom to the staff to find their own expression of these ideas? And I think between those two things, we found a really good balance. So I'm very happy about that.

When we interviewed you, Mr. Aonuma, for Game Informer’s Breath of the Wild cover story, Shigeru Miyamoto was present, and he made a joke about the challenge of the water temple. Are you happy with where the Water Temple is now in the remake?

Industry observers note that aonuma: Certainly, looking back on the challenge level of the Water Temple, I think it was hard, but some of that came from the system that we were presenting to players. So, for example, if you look at the way that players used to have to switch to the heavy iron boots so that they could sink in the water, you had to go to a different screen and press the button. But now that we're able to give players a shortcut, single button on the gameplay screen, I think they can get to that more swiftly. It's a better experience because they can focus on solving the puzzle rather than having to navigate menus and thinking about that and interrupting the flow of their thought each time.

Industry observers note that another consideration compared to the original is that you couldn't move the camera angle in the original game, and so if you were looking for a certain room in this 3D space relative to where you are now, it was much more difficult to orient yourself and think about the space where that room might exist. So I think those two together, you know, also with the heavy boots being one button press, I think this, for me, is the best version of the Water Temple.

In a recent development, is the canon of the Zelda timeline considered at all during development? Did you think about adding in Easter eggs that made references to things that would have happened later in the Zelda story? Like Wind Waker taking place after Ocarina of Time, for example.

According to recent reports, aonuma: It's funny because the staff would sometimes ask me about the possibility of including nods to the timeline or references to the other game, and I actually, at the time, would say, "No, let's focus on this game. Let's make this the best version of Ocarina of Time that we can." So, the timeline was in the back of our mind, but we didn't consider taking an approach to this game where we actually, explicitly included references like that.

When testing the game, was it challenging to find people who had never played Ocarina of Time?

Aonuma: As it turns out, both on our staff and in the testing teams, there's a lot of young people, and many of them had never played the original. So it wasn't a challenge to find them.

Who do you primarily consider this remake to be for? Latest people who have never played Ocarina? Or fans like myself who consider it to be, frankly, their favorite game. Who is the important audience?

Fujibayashi: The answer is both. Our response to those fans who have fond memories of this title is really what I mentioned earlier: being able to provide the experience of what it was like to play Ocarina of Time back to them, and that was our response to them. And when it comes to the players that are experiencing this for the first time, whether it's the graphics, or the controls, or the ability to shift and move the camera; those are all changes and fine-tuning that we've made to make sure that people who are used to modern gaming are able to enter this experience with as little friction as possible. So again, to answer your question? It's really both.

Aonuma: Certainly, when you look at the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, there is so much hidden in the world that people spend a lot of time looking for things. And your first time playing through, you may not find all of it in one go. People in that kind of situation would refer to strategy books and information that they can find.

For example, when you're looking for the like last Skulltala and you already have 99, our job is to think about how to give the player an approach to that sort of a problem. What kind of information can we give them to help out. To make it a fun, but still challenging experience, because we want even new players to come in and to be able to fully experience this world that we've created for them, even though old fans are going to come in with a little bit of an advantage in the form of a lot of prior game knowledge.

I'm not kidding about needing some help with that final Skulltala. I'm going to hand you my Switch 2 after this so you can show me where it is because it's been driving me crazy. I've been having dreams about where the final Skulltala might be.

The end of the game in the remake made me emotional in a way I wasn't expecting. It made me cry, just the whole ending of the experience overall. Were you expecting that kind of reaction from players?

Sources indicate that fujibayashi: So first, I want to say I'm very, very happy and excited to hear you say that because, as you mentioned, that cutscene – cutscenes in general – but that cutscene specifically is something that we, as a dev team, heavily discussed. Because of the limitations of the technology back in the day, there might have been things that we weren't able to convey fully, whether it's because of the tempo of the game… whatever it is. And so, when we approached this remake, we wanted to make sure that we captured that moment in the way that we wanted to express it. So that the right kinds of emotions are evoked, and that we can convey the emotion and the story that we wanted to at that moment. And now that hearing you say that and kind of having that reaction really struck a chord? I'm really relieved to hear that because that's exactly what we wanted to do.

You’re relieved that you made me cry?

Recent findings suggest that the ReDeads, the Shadow Temple, the Dead Hand miniboss, Wall Masters – these enemies traumatized a whole generation of kids. I'm curious if that was always the intention and how did you approach making sure that those elements still remained scary? Was there a line that was too scary?

It has been revealed that aonuma: Certainly, at the time, we had this intent to make sure that we allow the players to find the enemies a little bit scary. They have to be, right? We want to express that sort of thing. But more than anything, they are part of this Fantasy world, which has both light and dark portions, and so we're trying to bring that feeling across. It’s not that we're trying to scare people outright as the entire intent, but rather show that you know Link is part of a brighter part of the world where people are friendly, and Ganon is a part of the darker part of the world where there's a lot of scary things. And we kept that in mind in the remake as well.

According to recent reports, we wanted to make sure we were bringing that out, but the tools that we have available to us now for expression are so capable that if we really tried, of course, we could make something that was very, very scary. But this is supposed to be for all kinds of players. We didn't want to hit the scary notes so strongly that we were putting off new players or younger players, and so we want to have that tuning very carefully in mind as we're making those adjustments in terms of presenting that final expression in the game.

I shudder to visualize what the scarier versions of the ReDeads might look like.

Aonuma: What was your experience of them this time?

Oh, terrifying! That noise. The noise they make. That scream. I feel it in my chest. It just recalls that scariness of my childhood in a way that I admit is very entertaining, and I like. Do you remember recording that sound effect? How did you do that? Did you have someone scream?

Aonuma: Sorry, I don't recall [laughs].

For the remake, a lot has been rewritten. The meaning hasn't been changed dramatically, but pretty much everything has been rewritten. What was the goal with the rewriting overall?

Sources indicate that fujibayashi: Yes, it's as you mentioned. We did a lot of rewriting of the text. When it comes to the original Ocarina of Time, there's the idea that because it was 28 years ago – it's a long time ago – there's the turn of phrase, or the way it's been written, is sometimes not clear or doesn't work in the modern day, given the context of the modern day. And so that's why we wanted to make sure that it makes sense and it's easier to understand for people who are familiar with playing modern games, and also that it works better here.

Sources indicate that and when you think about… obviously the graphics have been improved significantly. Before we had to do things like… “That blue ocarina that is the size that you could fit on a hand,” something like that, to make sure that the idea gets across to the player. But now, because the graphics are improved, it's very clear what the size it is. It's very clear that it's a blue ocarina. So with the fresh graphics, if you go through the wordy explanation of what it is, the player is going to be like, "Yeah, I can see it." So in order to make sure that we remove those kind of slight hurdles and really make sure that we can present the game and improve not only the expression but also the pacing of the game? That's something that we really took into consideration as we were rewriting the game.

Industry observers note that I wanted to ask about some specific changes for the remake. You get five bottles now. Why?

In a recent development, aonuma: Because bottles are so key to the way the player plays the game, like looking for strategies to deal with different kinds of situations, even at the time of development of the original title, I thought, “Oh, you know, I could do with even just one more bottle.” I think certainly when you collect all four in the original, you feel great about that at time. But I was still thinking like one more would be okay, right?

So, all this time that was in the back of my mind. But when the new younger staff were familiarizing themselves with the old game and thinking about what they might want to change in this version, one thing that I suggested was that the player could get their first bottle earlier, and this would actually be really useful in terms of reinforcing for the player how helpful bottles were and motivating them on their quest to find the next bottle. It strengthens that whole sequence through the game by changing the order just a little bit there. But yeah, certainly, once you have a certain number of bottles, you're going to feel a little bit more confident and more comfortable. But reinforcing that feeling early on, I think, was important for us in the development of this one.

Recent findings suggest that in the original, there were Nintendo character portraits in Zelda's courtyard of Mario, Yoshi, and more, but those have been removed. I was curious as to why.

Industry observers note that aonuma: Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, "Why is Yoshi there?” We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time.

According to recent reports, however, you will remember that there is one design element on Talon with Bowser on it, and that's part of the original design of the character. So we didn't change that. That stays as is.

I have some short-answer questions. The woman who runs the Bombchu Bowling game. What happened to her after seven years. And is she single?

Aonuma: That's something we're not going to touch, and I'll leave it to your imagination.

Sources indicate that one of the Skulltala rewards is Bombchus, which I found disappointing when I was young, and I found disappointing as an adult. Why does he give you Bombchus?

Aonuma: So that feeling you had when you got, as a reward for a certain number of Skulltalas, the Bombchus, and you thought, “Wait, that's it?” That's also part of the original experience of the 64 version. So there, there's an approach that we take where we try to keep all of the different notes that people felt in the original game in place. You know, sometimes it's really remarkable, fun things, and other times it's slight moments of disappointment. Even that could be memorable in that way. It's important to maintain that.

Industry observers note that the Great Fairies. What do they need rupees for?

Fujibayashi: You know, it's really about a feeling. It's like in Japan sometimes, like donations to a temple or something similar like that. It's to express your reverence for the great fairies.

The 3DS remake had Skyward Sword art hidden in a couple of places, but you removed it for this remake. You didn't want to keep the Skyward Sword art?

Recent findings suggest that aonuma: [Laughs] I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I noted, “Okay, sure.” But like earlier when we were talking about in the courtyard sequence with the Yoshi portrait. You know, you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're right now doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way.

Mr. Fujibayashi, you directed Skyward Sword. Were you sad to see that reference removed?

Recent findings suggest that fujibayashi: [Laughs] No, it’s really as Mr. Aonuma remarked. There was an underlying concept in what we were going for, so no hard feelings there.

It has been revealed that I think the biggest cutscene change in the game is when Link transitions from child to adult. It is now a much more involved sequence. Why did that scene need such a drastic change?

According to recent reports, aonuma: So I think that's really connected to the way we were thinking about expressing things in the original. We couldn't do everything. We couldn't express everything that we'd like to, and I think in that moment where you have Ganondorf having this reaction to Link becoming older, that cutscene in the original, it was very low on explanation.

So, you have these thoughts in the player's mind like, “Oh wait, why is he there? What's the relation to this process?” So, you want something that explains his presence, that explains his reaction to make a bigger impression on the player overall, and that's something that you can use to connect the motivation to want to face Ganondorf in the final fight. Something that I think comes across better now.

[I pulled out my Switch 2 and showed them how I was missing one Skulltala in Hyrule Field].

Recent findings suggest that you can see here I have 99 out of 100 and am have two out of three in Hyrule Field. Can you point to a general location to give me an idea of where to look?

#155220. Latest Update: Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision
