Latest Update: Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field.
  • It has been revealed that an international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss.
  • Although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field. The condition may be especially difficult to recognize because people can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable problems develop.

It has been revealed that an international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss. However, the two diseases affect eyesight in strikingly different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, while the newly discovered condition affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness.

Although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD). It is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material between cells in the eye.

A Genetic Discovery That Began Decades Ago.

According to recent reports, the investigation traces back to 1998, when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As researchers uncovered new genetic evidence, they were able to connect those findings to families in Europe who showed similar symptoms.

The study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, examined three unrelated families from different countries who carried the p.Arg140Trp variant. Their symptoms were compared with those of another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the previously recognized disease affecting central vision.

The international collaboration included researchers from Penn Medicine, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Basel, Charles University, and the University of Bonn.

Recent findings suggest that at first, scientists suspected that the unusual symptoms in the original family might be caused by a different genetic disorder. Testing, however, failed to identify the variants responsible for that condition.

Industry observers note that "The different disease expression in this family was thought to be similar to a condition caused by C1QTNF5 gene variants. However, none of the variants associated with that disease were found," remarked Artur V. Cideciyan, PhD, an ophthalmology researcher and co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Our collaborators then discovered a new variant in the EFEMP1 gene that normally causes a different disease where the macula, which is tied to central vision, is affected first.".

How the Fresh Eye Disease Affects Night Vision.

The researchers found that the newly identified condition develops gradually in the outer regions of the retina. Located at the back of the eye, the retina detects incoming light and transforms it into signals that the brain uses to create visual images.

In a recent development, unlike the previously known EFEMP1 disorder, which initially affects the macula and central vision, this newly identified disease begins in the peripheral retina. People may see normally for much of their lives before gradually noticing that their side vision is narrowing or that seeing in dim surroundings has become more difficult.

Problems may be particularly noticeable around dusk or at night, when the eyes must rely more heavily on specialized light-sensitive cells called rods.

One reason the disease is challenging to diagnose is that these cells may initially show no visible structural damage. The gradual progression of symptoms can make the condition even harder to recognize.

However, the researchers identified a potentially valuable early clue. In affected individuals, rod cells take unusually long to recover when the eyes move from bright surroundings into darkness. This abnormal response can be detected even when the retina still appears structurally normal.

It has been revealed that "We can detect a major abnormality in the way rod photoreceptors recover in darkness with retinas that still look structurally intact," Cideciyan said. "This gives us a functional marker of disease at a stage when photoreceptor cells have not yet been lost.".

The finding suggests that changes in how the retina functions may reveal the disease before the light-sensitive cells responsible for vision begin to disappear.

What the Discovery Could Mean for Age-Related Vision Loss.

An notable question remains unanswered: How many people carry this newly identified genetic variant?

It has been revealed that researchers suspect the condition is relatively uncommon, but they do not yet have enough information to determine its prevalence. Larger investigations will be necessary to establish how frequently the variant occurs and how many people may be affected.

Beyond identifying another inherited eye disorder, the findings could help scientists better understand why vision deteriorates with age. Studying rare genetic diseases can reveal biological processes that may also contribute to much more widespread retinal conditions.

Sources indicate that "Aging is a risk factor for many medical conditions, including retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, the most common retinal condition of aging," noted Tomas S. Aleman, MD, a professor of ophthalmology and the other co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Lessons learned from these infrequent, late-onset genetic eye diseases offer glimpses at possible mechanisms of disease for much more frequent retinal problems.".

By revealing how different changes in a single gene can produce distinct patterns of vision loss, the research adds to scientists' understanding of inherited retinal disease. It also highlights the potential importance of detecting changes in visual function before damage becomes apparent in the retina's structure.

The study received support from the University of Edinburgh Chancellor's Fellowship award, RS Macdonald Charitable Trust Seedcorn Award, the BrightFocus Foundation (M2024009N), the German Research Foundation (532367710), the Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00035/9, MC_UU_00007/10), the Swiss National Science Foundation (204285), the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic (NW24-06-00083), Charles University in Prague (UNCE/24/MED/022 and SVV 2600631), and the Samuel G. Jacobson, MD, PhD, Memorial Fund.

Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • Industry observers note that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Industry observers note that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

It has been revealed that zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Recent findings suggest that zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

It has been revealed that zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA remarked in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he highlighted up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

#155215. The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 Remake

The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 Remake

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?).
  • According to recent reports, in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game.
  • For the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?). Now in its second remake, not every secret has made its way forward through the previous iterations, but many have. Below you will learn about a few of the secrets that made the cut, and others that didn’t.

According to recent reports, in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game. If you don’t rush to Zelda and instead pause and enter first-person to look around, you will see portraits of other Nintendo characters through the windows, like Mario and Yoshi. In the 3DS remake, the portraits are replaced by an image of a Mario stage.

For the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters. Instead, the tapestry you build over the course of the game is on display. Removing the reference to Nintendo characters outside of the Zelda universe is understandable, but it is a little odd that art representing the full adventure of the game – an adventure that has not yet concluded – is on the wall.

As stated above, the Nintendo character portraits are gone, but there is still a guard you can annoy. If you fire a Deku Seed into the left window, a guard will pop out, yell at you, and then throw a bomb at you. You can’t pick up the bomb. In fact, at this point in the game, you haven’t even seen a bomb.

It has been revealed that the Hyrule Castle portrait references to Yoshi and Mario are gone (though Mario and Luigi are still kind of in the game in a way), but Bowser gets a pass for some reason. Both Malon and her dad, Talon, are still wearing Bowser pins on their clothes. And unlike the N64 game where the detail was a little vague, there is no mistaking it here.

In a recent development, gossip Stones are all over Ocarina of Time and it takes a while to understand what they do. If you hit them with a sword, they tell you the time, and if you play Zelda’s Lullaby near them, they refill your magic. If you do the Happy Mask Salesman’s side quest, interacting with them while wearing the Mask of Truth offers little hints and details about the world. But then there are interactions that are just odd for no reason. Blowing up a bomb near a Gossip Stone still makes it take off like a rocket ship, and using the Megaton Hammer still flattens them for a moment like a Looney Tunes.

And speaking of playing Zelda’s Lullaby for inanimate objects, if you slash a sign to pieces with your sword and regret your words and deeds, you can play the iconic tune to make the signs reform and become readable again.

It has been revealed that this detail was exclusive to the 3DS remake of Ocarina of Time, and surprising no one, it has been removed. Ocarina of Time introduced in June 2011 and Nintendo released Skyward Sword about five months later in November. For… marketing purposes, I guess, Skyward Sword art could be found in Lonlon Ranch, the Bombchu Shop in Hyrule Castle Town, and the Gerudo Fortress. It was a fun Easter Egg to discover back in 2011, especially since Skyward Sword was still months away, but these days it’s a bit of an odd inclusion.

Though never explicit, the composer ghosts guarding the Sun’s Song (and Link’s first ReDead encounter) have always been assumed to be inspired by Mario and Luigi. They are brothers; Flat is short, squat, and red; Sharp is lanky and green. They still appear in Ocarina of Time this way, which isn't surprising, since they are notable characters you must meet to get a very useful song. Fans have also speculated that Talon and Ingo are Mario and Luigi-inspired for similar reasons, but it’s worth noting that they are not brothers.

According to recent reports, in the Spirit Temple there is a large statue of a woman and for reasons that have never been explained, Link could attach his hookshot to her breasts. It served no purpose. It didn’t help solve a puzzle. If anything, it was confusing. But we all tried it and there is no shame in admitting it! That was removed for the 3DS remake, and it remains removed in 2026.

This is a very subtle reference to Wind Waker/Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom and is potentially the only addition to the remake that looks toward the future of the Zelda franchise. Obviously, plenty of characters in Ocarina later appear in Majora’s Mask (another remake of that is hopefully being considered), but it would be inaccurate to call those intentional Easter Eggs.

Industry observers note that however, in Kokiri Forest and in the neighboring Lost Woods, the magical debris floating in the air often resembles a Korok as it would later appear in the series. It makes sense, too, because the Koroks are meant to be what the Kokiri transformed into following The Great Flood.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The sun will come out tomorrow…maybe.

It's all about descending into the darkness and discovering what lies in its depths in this week's Ahead of the Game series, where we tell you about a newly introduced mobile endeavour that's playable in one form or another despite its unofficial launch.

The idea of descending into the depths of the unknown is already terrifying as it is, but in Sol Cesto, you're doing so because the sun has mysteriously disappeared - and all manner of unholy creatures have taken over because of it.

I've always been a fan of roguelikes, so the genre alone already scores points in my book. But I suppose what makes Sol Cesto even more interesting are the visuals - in some ways, it reminds me of this Burton-esque puzzler, Jars, with its creepy-but-cute charm.

Now, there's absolutely nothing cute about the monsters in the dungeons here, but it's still pretty compelling to dive into the depths to take them on. The randomised elements come in grids and stages, where you can use rewards you earn to, as you might expect, strengthen your hero when you head back up to the surface after inevitably perishing.

You unlock more heroes as you go along too, with each one offering their own sets of skills depending on your play style.

In a recent development, the haunting music adds to the atmosphere, so if you're looking for horror-adjacent roguelike runs before rushing into December, this might just do the trick. So, how do you play Sol Cesto? It's presently got that "early access" tag on Google Play, but I'm curious as to what else Snapbreak is cooking up behind the scenes before this is officially introduced. It's all pretty hush-hush at the moment, though, so if you want to get your hands on Sol Cesto before it's actually announced, now's your chance!

Latest Update: A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1168 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension.
  • Sources indicate that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile.
  • The findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

Sources indicate that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a fresh study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

The findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

The research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

"We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," says Cohen. "The scope of this new analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.".

AI Analysis Reveals Latest Benefits of Brown Fat.

To investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

In a recent development, the team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover important details about brown fat and its effects on health.

Nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

The analysis revealed that brown fat's location could be just as important as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

"For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he claims. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers.".

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat.

In a recent development, as the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

According to recent reports, to explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

In a recent development, even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

"The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," says Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure.".

In a recent development, additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan demonstrated increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health.

Industry observers note that beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric complications," indicates Gómez-Banoy.

The researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

However, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

The discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

Losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

"There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that somehow, after all these years, there are still a considerable number of vehicles equipped with Takata airbags, though their number should be considerably lower in the near future. Honda just issued a recall for 810,592 cars equipped with Takata airbags that could rupture due to propellant degradation caused by high humidity.

According to documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the recall covers some 2013 Acura RDX, ILX, Honda CR-V, Civic, and Accord models. The affected Accords and Acuras are all from the 2013 model year, while the CR-V and Civic populations include both 2012 and 2013 vehicles.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21215.

Industry observers note that the NHTSA documents show that the affected vehicles are equipped with airbag inflators that use a phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate propellant, which is intended to control moisture within the inflator. Over time, exposure to high humidity and repeated temperature changes can cause the inflator to become brittle. When the brittle inflators are deployed, they could turn into projectiles that shoot metal fragments through the cabin, potentially injuring or killing occupants.

The recall comes after years of investigation and analysis by Honda, which was routinely shared with NHTSA. The recall documents show that on November 19, 2026, Honda determined that the inflators posed enough of a risk to warrant the new recall.

Owners of affected models will be contacted by mail and urged to bring their vehicle to a Honda or Acura dealership. Dealer technicians will replace the driver and passenger airbag inflators with a different model for free. Dealers have already been notified of the recall, with owner notification letters scheduled to be sent on December 18. Owners concerned that their car might be included in the recall can check on the NHTSA recalls site as well as NHTSA’s dedicated Takata airbag recall page.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

It has been revealed that all around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the fresh Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I promptly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

It has been revealed that after hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

According to recent reports, if you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the upcoming free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

It has been revealed that if you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Industry observers note that navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

Recent findings suggest that and the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is new for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

In a recent development, even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

Breaking: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout.
  • The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues.
  • According to recent reports, depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly important for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health.

According to recent reports, depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to new academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an important research priority.

Although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

According to recent reports, to investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

Industry observers note that at the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity.

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise revealed the same relationship with mental health.

Exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

It has been revealed that the researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week indicated a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health.

Taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an crucial part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Industry observers note that even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

According to recent reports, the authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life.".

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an important part of a healthy learning environment.".

In a recent development, funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

Less than three weeks after Nintendo debuted its highly-anticipated The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Nintendo Switch 2, PC customers are working hard to prove why they’re the master race by transforming the game entirely with an immersive upcoming VR mode.

The mod, known as OcarinaVR, was developed by ReTracedGames and builds upon the previously released PC port. It is showing the true skills of the PC modding community, and at what speed they can work to develop player experiences beyond a game’s original console boundaries.

Sources indicate that the power of the OcarinaVR mod is quite the sight to behold. It goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective with accurate spatial scaling—meaning the world adjusts depending on whether the player is controlling young Link or the grown-up version.

According to recent reports, the mod also brings intricate control mechanics and hand tracking, allowing players to map and control Link’s arms and individual fingers using their VR controllers. Swinging the Master sword and bashing enemies with the Hylian shield never looks so satisfying and adds a sense of depth and realism to the game beyond just its graphics.

Sources indicate that ocarinaVR also manages UI elements and prevents clutter, displaying HUD readouts like heart count and the minimap as floating panels. Pre-rendered cutscenes are displayed on a curved virtual cinema screen for maximum immersion as the perspective shifts back to the 3rd person.

OcarinaVR … goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective.

According to recent reports, the mod is based on the Hookshot PC recompilation that was released on PC shortly after Ocarina of Time introduced on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. That release already brought native widescreen and uncapped framerates, meaning it was a solid foundation for the OcarinaVR mod to build off.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental, with players praising its highly-detailed graphics and faithful retelling of the classic Zelda tale. Critics loved it equally as much, giving it one of the highest ratings on Metacritic of all time—a solid 95/100 aggregated score.

In DualShockers’ own review, Tayna Garcia wrote that the remake gives returning players an “opportunity to experience those same feelings again” from their childhoods, powered by nostalgia, but said it's a perfect place for newcomers to start their Zelda journey, too.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental [and] critics loved it equally as much.

Recent findings suggest that the game was swiftly followed by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6—perhaps the most hyped game of all time (and the highest reviewed on Metacritic with a stunning score of 99). Nintendo knew to get Zelda out the door before the news cycle and social media turned to GTA 6 for who knows how long.

The new VR mod gives fans a chance to take on Ocarina of Time in a whole new way, snatching a little bit of attention back from the Vice City-drenched mediascape right now.

Can Pirelli’s Cyber Tyre Technology Replace Drive Modes?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout.
  • It has been revealed that that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data.
  • "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout. The tires use a sensor that looks a lot like a Dexcom G7 to feed temperature, air pressure, acceleration, and identification data to a vehicle's computers.

It has been revealed that that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data. For example, swap your summer tires for squishier winter rubber, and a compatible car could recognize the change and automatically adjust how its electronic controls intervene, leaving you free to imagine a world where maybe we all just drove better.

See all results for used cars for sale near 64850.

"This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani. The sensor, weighing just 13 grams, is bonded to the tire's inner liner beneath the tread using a specially developed adhesive and rubber housing. The process was developed using learnings from Pirelli's Noise Cancelling System, which uses foam inside the tire to absorb sound waves and reduce cabin vibration. The sensor must survive extreme temperatures, constant flexing, and the insane lateral g-forces that tires are susceptible to at over 200 mph. Engineers explained that its battery is designed to outlast the tire and enters a low-power sleep mode during extended storage.

The more inspiring part is what the car does with the information it gathers. As we found in our recent all-weather tire comparison test, summer, winter, and all-season tires perform dramatically differently. Yet a vehicle's electronic controls are generally calibrated around its original equipment, using things like wheel speed sensors that aren’t as close to the road surface as the Cyber Tyre. Instead, it identifies the specific tire installed at each corner, allowing it to use different wheel-slip targets. And with the sensor attached to the inside of the tire, the data informing those systems is closer to the road surface than ever.

We sampled the technology at Las Vegas Motor Speedway in two Mercedes-AMG GT63 S four-doors wearing Cyber Tyre-equipped P Zero MS all-season tires.

According to recent reports, the first exercise had us pin the throttle through a corner from 40 mph using three different traction-control calibrations, all on the same P Zero MS all-season tires. The first, intended for ultra-high-performance summer tires, was overly restrictive, cutting power before the tires could deliver much acceleration. The second, calibrated for winter tires, permitted considerably more wheelspin, making the AMG easy to slide. Despite that setting being the most fun (and our favorite), Cyber Tyre delivered a happy medium, allowing more controlled acceleration without either extreme.

See all results for used cars for sale near 64850.

This is where Cyber Tyre begins to make the case against selectable drive modes. The same car, wearing the same tires, just behaved three different ways without any mechanical changes. It's not going to replace the button that stiffens your dampers or changes your exhaust note, but it could eventually make some traction-related settings redundant.

It has been revealed that the second AMG demonstrated ABS braking from 65 mph. With Cyber Tyre integration active, our stopping distance improved by 0.9 meter, or about three feet, according to Pirelli's instrumentation. That's not dramatically different, but still a measurable improvement.

Sources indicate that of course, these demonstrations weren't proof that Cyber Tyre can outperform a conventional system already calibrated for the correct tires. And the technology isn't smart enough to know it's snowing just because the tires are cold. But the distinction is that Cyber Tyre can give the car information about its tires without the driver doing anything. That could be super useful as tires wear, temperatures change, or owners swap between summer and winter sets. Pirelli is also developing tire-wear estimates using its sensor data, which could prove useful for fleet operators managing hundreds of vehicles.

In a recent development, pirelli and Bosch announced their development partnership in 2024, and the technology has already appeared in vehicles from McLaren and Pagani. Pirelli executives say a substantially higher-volume application should be announced in the first half of 2027, with production expected in 2028. So it's possible this tech could arrive in models as common as a Ford pickup.

According to recent reports, pirelli is also investing approximately $1.2 billion to expand its Rome, Georgia, manufacturing facility, where Cyber Tyre-equipped products will be produced alongside conventional tires. By 2033, the company expects annual production capacity to reach six million tires and looks to add up to 1000 engineering jobs.

They also recently announced that China's state-owned Sinochem, formerly Pirelli's largest shareholder, reduced its ownership to 13.6 percent in November. The Italian government has restricted Sinochem's influence and specifically prohibited sharing Cyber Tyre data with entities connected to the Chinese government. Following those governance changes, Pirelli received U.S. authorization to market the technology here. Not that anyone was worried about a Pagani Utopia Roadster being a boon of classified information.

It has been revealed that cyber Tyre isn't about to take the Ford Bronco's G.O.A.T. modes out back to shoot them. There are plenty of reasons to let drivers decide how their cars behave. But after experiencing three dramatically different calibrations in the same AMG, it's easy to see why some of those decisions might eventually be better left to the car. Just make sure we’re able to fully disable them.

In a recent development, austin Irwin has worked for Car and Driver for over 10 years in various roles. He's steadily worked his way from an entry-level data entry position into driving vehicles for photography and video, and is now reviewing and testing cars. What will he do next? Who knows, but he better be fast.

Breaking: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a fresh clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating.
  • The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes.
  • Sources indicate that "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a fresh clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

Sources indicate that "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have key therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone.".

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets.

Industry observers note that an estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

Three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

Sources indicate that these eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

To compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss.

Participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating plans, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

The diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

According to recent reports, researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

Recent findings suggest that by the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

Keto Diet Reduces Liver Fat by 67%.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several important indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

Participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

The ketogenic group highlighted the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

Sources indicate that one result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," states Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes.

It has been revealed that the benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

These differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an vital improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

The findings also highlight a potentially vital distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

Researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful new obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

Industry observers note that "GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen indicates. "But in addition, our study highlights that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits.".

In a recent development, although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an important role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience introduces today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

It has been revealed that the beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

Sources indicate that the Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as swiftly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

According to recent reports, the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two upcoming additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

The tech giant name-dropped Banjo-Kazooie in the post beside its hugely successful IPs … igniting speculation online.

The pair’s most recent outing was as DLC characters for Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, and they saw a nostalgic return through Nintendo Switch Online ports. But no original content has been developed for the IP in years, and the game’s original developer, Rare, is now under the Xbox / Activision umbrella of studios.

The Project Manager job listing indicates the latest role will feature defining and driving “the publishing product strategy” for premium console and PC titles—verbiage which certainly indicates that Banjo-Kazooie might be getting a new push on modern platforms. But whether it’s just a red herring, or Activision trying to show off the feathers in its cap, fans are unsure.

In a recent development, under the leadership of XBOX’s CEO Asha Sharma, the gaming giant has been shifting its focus towards nostalgia plays—much like other entertainment mediums, from TV to movies. There’s a lot of money to be made in the wistful feelings of rosy days gone by, and Sharma’s announcements have made it clear that the organization aims to work hard to earn that slice of the pie.

Under the leadership of XBOX’s CEO Asha Sharma, the gaming giant has been shifting its focus towards nostalgia plays.

The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

Industry observers note that with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to Upcoming York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

Sources indicate that ocarina of Time is easily one of the most vital video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Sources indicate that taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

Industry observers note that and my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

Sources indicate that and then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) fresh years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are right now working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

Sources indicate that this, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Sources indicate that understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s newly introduced ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of fresh Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).
