U.S. loses measles elimination status after 25 years as vaccine myths persist

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1309 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years, marking a major setback in the fight against a highly contagious disease.
  • It has been revealed that the United States first achieved measles elimination status in 2000.
  • It has been revealed that the announcement comes during the country's worst measles resurgence in decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years, marking a major setback in the fight against a highly contagious disease. At the same time, a new nationwide survey from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) reveals that many Americans remain confused about the dangers of measles and the vaccines that protect against it.

It has been revealed that the United States first achieved measles elimination status in 2000. This designation meant that no strain of the virus had spread continuously within the country for 12 months or longer. However, on Nov. 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization confirmed that the United States no longer qualified for that status.

It has been revealed that the announcement comes during the country's worst measles resurgence in decades. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the United States had recorded 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026 as of Nov. 12. That is more than twice the 2,290 cases reported throughout all of 2025.

Vaccine Myths Persist Despite Decades of Scientific Evidence.

In a recent development, A November 2026 Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) survey, conducted using adults from the SSRS Omnibus survey, highlights widespread misunderstandings about childhood vaccination. Nearly two-thirds of Americans (64%) correctly rejected the claim that "vaccines given to children for diseases like measles, mumps, and rubella cause autism." However, 17% believed the claim was true, while another 19% noted they did not know whether it was true or false.

Recent findings suggest that the results closely resemble findings from earlier APPC research. Across four surveys involving a separate sample of U.S. adults (September 2024 to August 2026), the ongoing ASAPH national probability survey found that 65% to 68% correctly rejected a connection between childhood vaccines and autism (65%-68%). Another 12% to 14% incorrectly believed there was a connection (12%-14%), while 19% to 22% remained uncertain.

The latest survey also asked respondents to compare autism rates among fully vaccinated and unvaccinated children. Nearly half (49%) believed both groups were "about as likely" to show signs of autism. Another 11% thought fully vaccinated children were "more likely" to show signs, 14% believed they were "less likely," and 26% could not say.

Industry observers note that extensive scientific research has found no evidence that vaccines cause autism. In 2004, the National Academy of Medicine (then named the Institute of Medicine) concluded that "the body of epidemiological evidence favors rejection of a causal relationship between the MMR vaccine and autism evidence.".

The World Health Organization's Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety reached the same conclusion in 2025, reaffirming that high-quality scientific evidence does not establish a causal relationship between vaccination and autism. FactCheck.org, which is operated by the Annenberg Public Policy Center, has also challenged claims linking vaccines to autism, explaining that the evidence does not support them.

In a recent development, these misconceptions may have consequences for vaccination decisions. Previous Annenberg research found that people who accept false vaccine claims, including the belief that the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine causes autism, are less likely to recommend MMR vaccination to people who are eligible to receive it.

Only 9% of Americans Know How Deadly Measles Can Be.

Industry observers note that the survey uncovered another striking knowledge gap. Most Americans appear uncertain about the risk of death associated with measles in children.

When asked how many children infected with measles are likely to die from the disease, 59% of respondents said they did not know. Just 9% selected the correct response, "about 1 in 1,000," which most closely matches the CDC’s estimate that 1 to 3 of every 1,000 infected children die from respiratory or neurological complications.

Nearly one-quarter of respondents (23%) underestimated the death rate, while another 9% selected a higher rate.

Knowledge about measles vaccination was also limited. Almost half of Americans (49%) noted they were unsure how many doses children need for full protection. Only about one-third (34%) correctly identified the recommended two-dose schedule.

The CDC advises giving children their first MMR vaccine dose between 12 and 15 months of age, followed by a second dose between ages 4 and 6. According to CDC data, a single dose provides 93% protection against measles, while receiving both doses increases effectiveness to 97%.

According to recent reports, public Confidence in Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Remains Low.

The survey also examined Americans' trust in U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The findings indicate that public confidence in his health-related communications has changed little since earlier surveys conducted in 2025 and 2026.

According to recent reports, in November 2026, about six in 10 respondents (61%) stated they were not confident that Kennedy was providing trustworthy information about public health. The remaining four in 10 (39%) expressed confidence in the information he provides.

It has been revealed that these results are consistent with seven earlier national probability surveys conducted over two years (February 2025 to August 2026). During that period, 60% to 63% of respondents reported lacking confidence in Kennedy, while 37% to 39% expressed confidence.

Kathleen Hall Jamieson, director of the Annenberg Public Policy Center's Science of Science Communication Institute and its ASAPH and ASK surveys, mentioned the loss of measles elimination status demonstrates the consequences of declining vaccination coverage.

Industry observers note that "The announcement that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status confirms what we already knew," said Kathleen Hall Jamieson. "Those who refused the MMR vaccine for themselves or their children and those who misled them into doing so have produced the tragic effects that science predicted would occur when community immunity dropped below the threshold needed to protect those who are not able to be vaccinated or refused to be.".

How the National Measles Survey Was Conducted.

The findings draw on two types of Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) surveys.

In a recent development, the November 2026 results come from a nationally representative survey of 1,028 U.S. adults conducted for APPC by SSRS, an independent market research organization. Participants were selected from the company's probability-based online opinion panel, and responses were collected Nov. 6-8, 2026. The survey has a margin of sampling error (MOE) of ± 3.5 percentage points at the 95% confidence level.

The other findings come from APPC's ongoing ASAPH panel surveys, which are also administered by SSRS. Participants were originally recruited through probability sampling from the SSRS Opinion Panel, and their responses are weighted to reflect the U.S. adult population. This research panel operates separately from the SSRS Omnibus survey and has completed more than 30 survey waves since April 2021.

Percentages are rounded to the nearest whole number, so totals may not always equal 100%.

Industry observers note that additional results are available in the survey topline, which includes data from both the November 2026 omnibus survey and the ongoing ASAPH panel surveys. A separate methodology statement provides further details about the latest survey.

Since April 2021, the Annenberg Public Policy Center has used its Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) research program and separate national samples to monitor Americans' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to vaccines, Covid-19, influenza, RSV, and other important health concerns.

The APPC health survey team includes Ken Winneg, managing director of survey research; Laura A. Gibson, research analyst; and Patrick E. Jamieson, director of the Annenberg Health and Risk Communication Institute.

Materials provided by Annenberg Public Policy Center of the University of Pennsylvania. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • It has been revealed that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Organization of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

It has been revealed that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell notes. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

According to recent reports, just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

It has been revealed that as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

In a recent development, anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Firm of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell states. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

It has been revealed that relic and latest owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Manufacturer of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and confirmed they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very rapidly.".

I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had intends to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a substantial part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

In a recent development, as to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are, quite literally, millions of people playing GTA 6, as Rockstar revealed its hit fresh game sold more than 32 million copies on its first day. That means the solitary player to have unlocked the game’s Platinum Trophy on PS5 is, quite literally, one in more than 32 million at this moment in time.

PSNProfiles is a website that tracks the trophy stats for every PlayStation game, both for personal use if you want to check in on your own milestones, and as a collective so you can see how you measure up against everyone else.

That means it’s the best place to go to see exactly how many people have unlocked a game’s Platinum rather than going by the rough percentage you’re shown on a game’s actual trophy list. It’s particularly helpful in GTA 6’s case, as that percentage is still locked at zero, but there’s actually one player who has managed to unlock it.

According to recent reports, according to PSNProfiles, that world first has been achieved by a player who goes by Danpool85. It also shows that they’ve been playing the game for over a week, which means they had a head start on most of those 32 million who have only been playing for four days. Either they bent the rules or, the more likely scenario, they were provided a review copy early by Rockstar.

They really are the only one right now, too. The Xbox equivalent of PSNProfiles, TrueAchievements, is still showing a zero when it comes to how many players have unlocked GTA 6’s Mythic Achievement. Mythic is the new Platinum-equivalent Xbox achievement added very recently, turning all of those 1,000 Gamerscores into Mythics, dating all the way back to the 360, and seemingly even a few original Xbox titles.

Sources indicate that there are 55 trophies to unlock in GTA 6, and its Platinum isn’t currently the only one with so few unlocks that they’re still claiming no one has unlocked them. Performing 250 stunts is another trophy that barely anyone has, as is the trophy you get for scanning 100 different objects using your WAiNK app.

Even though there’s still so much more left to do and see, as demonstrated by literally one person in the world reaching 100% completion so far, some of the secrets the millions of us playing have collectively discovered so far are nothing short of incredible.

In less than a week, players have already managed to stop the GTA 6 train - something that was infamously impossible in previous entries - and discovered an easter egg that mentions the GTA 5 protagonists by name, confirming the games take place in the same shared universe. The tip of the hat to the last GTA can be found in a GTA 6 true crime podcast where the host interviews Wade, another character from GTA 5. Wade comments on Trevor, Franklin, and Michael not being responsible for the murders of Deborah and Floyd, blissfully unaware that they did kill those characters and then framed him for their murders.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

Industry observers note that the massive new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

In a recent development, as with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

Tech Report: Mice slept 70% less after scientists switched off these brain cells

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that why does being awake for too long make us increasingly desperate for sleep?
  • The longer we go without sleep, the more difficult it becomes to stay awake.
  • Researchers led by Professor Alex Schier at the Biozentrum, University of Basel, have now identified brain cells that help regulate this process.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that why does being awake for too long make us increasingly desperate for sleep? Scientists at the University of Basel in Switzerland have identified two groups of brain cells in mice that become more active the longer the animals remain awake. These neurons play a critical role in creating the pressure to sleep, offering newly introduced clues about how the brain regulates our need for rest.

The longer we go without sleep, the more difficult it becomes to stay awake. This buildup of sleep pressure, often called sleep drive, helps ensure that extended periods of wakefulness are followed by longer and deeper sleep. Although sleep is essential for survival, exactly how the brain measures time spent awake and converts that information into an increasing need for sleep has remained a mystery.

Researchers led by Professor Alex Schier at the Biozentrum, University of Basel, have now identified brain cells that help regulate this process. The work was conducted in collaboration with scientists from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Auburn University.

"We have identified neuronal populations that monitor prolonged wakefulness and actively promote sleep," notes Alex Schier. "This is an important missing piece of the puzzle in understanding why we become sleepy.".

Scientists Identify Brain Cells That Drive Sleep Pressure.

To investigate how sleep pressure develops, the team studied patterns of brain activity in mice under three different conditions: normal cycles of sleeping and waking, extended sleep deprivation, and recovery sleep. By comparing these patterns, they identified brain regions whose activity changed according to how long the animals had been awake.

According to recent reports, within one of these regions, the brainstem, researchers pinpointed two groups of neurons involved in controlling sleep drive. Known as GABAergic and serotonergic neurons, both groups became progressively more active as the mice remained awake. Their activity then decreased once the animals fell asleep.

The next question was whether these neurons simply tracked how long the mice had been awake or actually helped create the growing need for sleep.

Experiments revealed that the neurons were directly involved in driving sleep. When researchers artificially activated both groups, the mice slept longer and more deeply, showing the same type of recovery sleep normally seen after extended wakefulness. When the neurons were inhibited, however, the animals slept substantially less and were able to remain awake and alert.

Industry observers note that "These neurons do not simply signal that an animal has been awake," says Schier. "Our experiments show that they are crucial to promote sleep, and that they may be key components of the neural circuitry that generates sleep drive.".

The results provide particularly strong evidence that certain neurons activated during wakefulness do more than register lost sleep. They actively help generate the pressure that eventually pushes the brain toward sleep.

Mice Sleep 70% Less When Key Neurons Are Inhibited.

Industry observers note that further experiments produced an especially surprising result. When scientists suppressed both groups of neurons for an extended period, the mice slept approximately 70% less than normal.

Even more unexpectedly, most of these animals did not display some of the serious behavioral problems typically associated with prolonged sleep deprivation. Despite getting dramatically less sleep, many avoided impairments that researchers would ordinarily expect.

These findings suggest that the identified neurons influence not only the amount of time animals spend sleeping, but also how strongly the pressure to sleep increases during wakefulness.

Rather than simply responding to exhaustion, the brain appears to use specific neural circuits to actively regulate the growing need for rest.

A Upcoming Direction for Sleep Research.

Recent findings suggest that understanding these circuits could open crucial newly introduced avenues for studying sleep and its effects on the body. Researchers now hope to determine how the identified neurons communicate with other brain regions and what molecular processes allow them to generate sleep pressure.

It has been revealed that "Future studies could reveal how these neurons interact with the rest of the brain, and how sleep drive is generated at the molecular level," says Dr. William Joo, first author of the study. "Our ability to stably transform sleep behavior also allows us to explore adaptations to long-term sleep loss - this may eventually reveal ways to confer resilience to sleep deprivation and other physiological challenges.".

The findings establish that GABAergic and serotonergic neurons in the brainstem become increasingly active during prolonged wakefulness and play an essential role in promoting sleep.

Determining exactly how the brain makes sleep increasingly difficult to resist remains a major objective of sleep research. Beyond improving scientists' understanding of sleep disorders, this discovery could help explain how the nervous system adapts to extended wakefulness and other physical challenges.

Ultimately, a clearer understanding of the brain circuits responsible for sleep pressure could inspire new treatments and potentially reveal ways to improve resilience to sleep deprivation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

Sources indicate that I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Industry observers note that presently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is released over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

In a recent development, I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

It has been revealed that the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

It has been revealed that casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

Recent findings suggest that I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that said it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

It has been revealed that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

The prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • There are a lot of good starter cars to register out there, but once you’re ready to expand, you might want something a little different.
  • Every vehicle on this list serves a good purpose and won’t run you into the ground money-wise, which is a nice bonus given your bank account problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vehicles can be tough to come by in the early hours of GTA 6, and it doesn’t get much easier the farther into the game you get. Most every car you get has to be stolen in one way or another, especially after unlocking some new personal vehicles.

There are a lot of good starter cars to register out there, but once you’re ready to expand, you might want something a little different. You won’t have an infinite amount of money, so you’ll need to be a little picky about what you want to keep.

Every vehicle on this list serves a good purpose and won’t run you into the ground money-wise, which is a nice bonus given your bank account problems. These are most of the general vehicles you can find around Port Gellhorn, although a couple are special finds.

Sometimes it’s nice to just have something a little fancy that’ll ride nice and easy down the streets. This Lowrider is by no means the faster or toughest car around, and it’s fairly average all around.

In a recent development, that’s what makes it a good extra car to have, because it’s fairly decent at everything. If you get it suped up, it can get much better, but since money is tight, it’s a relatively cheap option to buy, saving you some much-needed cash.

This one is a ton of fun to drive, mostly because it’s a pretty speedy vehicle on asphalt, but not so much on dirt. That’s really what drags the car down, but still it’s a nice car that’ll get you most anywhere in a jiffy.

According to recent reports, if you’re a bit accident-prone, or prone to running into crazy NPCs, you may want to find something a bit sturdier. Still, it looks good and runs smoothly on asphalt, so it’s definitely one of the better vehicles on the road.

Sources indicate that this car is a bit of an oddball for the area, as it’s clearly more of an upper-middle-class family car, which is not exactly what you think of in Port Gellhorn. It’s not a bad car for moving from point to point on the road or dirt.

Recent findings suggest that it’s got pretty good handling and has some good size to it, making a good car for taking up space on the road. You won’t have to worry too much about getting hit with this massive boy backing you up.

There are a lot of crazy looking cars on the road in GTA, but this is mostly a pretty normal-looking car. That remarked, it still can get going on the open road without wasting too much time, so as a getaway vehicle it’s not a bad choice.

It’s on the cheaper side and seemingly pretty abundant, so getting one shouldn’t be too difficult at this point in the game. The only real problem with the vehicle is that it’s got limited handling on both dirt and asphalt.

For the most part, you’re going to want a car over a bike, but when the moment for a bike comes, the Enduro is a great choice. It’s great for making a quick getaway on the road, provided you don’t crash into anything.

This one handles surprisingly nicely, but since it is a bike, you’re in a much more dangerous position to get hurt in an accident. Sounds silly, but when you’re holding a bag full of goodies, it’s not fun to lose it.

In a recent development, this is one chunky vehicle, but in a game like this, that comes in handy. It’s not bad on any terrain, and it can get up to speed pretty quickly, making it an excellent vehicle to go on a stealing spree with.

It has been revealed that it can take a hit as good as it gives one, but its overall size might make squeezing through some tight streets a little difficult. It’s able to just move people out of the way with ease, but we all know that brings out the crazies.

Recent findings suggest that while you’re mostly going to want something for the road in the early days, getting something that can do both is helpful. It’s not great on the road, but better than most, and it takes off from zero pretty swiftly.

The major problem is that road handling is terrible, and the overall speed drops off pretty swiftly; still, if you need to get off the road, this thing is great. You can even abuse it a bit since it’s a little stronger than most vehicles.

The Outlaw is one of the best and easiest-to-get vehicles in the game; while it might not be as nice as Paul Walker’s car, it does the job. Clearly a four-wheeler made for running off the road and making your own path.

Recent findings suggest that it’s surprisingly good on both the dirt and road, but especially in the dirt, you can basically go wherever you want. It’s a beast, especially if you’re making your way through the swampy areas. It’s a bit expensive, but well worth the price.

Recent findings suggest that one of the special vehicles you can find in a gang territory, this Caracara 4X4 is a phenomenal vehicle that really does it all. It’s got everything you might need in the early hours, and with some bonus strength, you can really push people around.

It has been revealed that the only weak spot it has is that its asphalt handling is pretty bad, but who needs a road when you can just make your own? It’s a great car to keep Jason and Lucia happy and safe, without risking too much from either of them.

Another special vehicle you can steal from a gang hideout, the Firebug Dominator is an absolute godsend early on in the game. It’s got quick acceleration and some terrifying speed that’s only enhanced by the free nitro boost it comes with.

If there’s any car you need to have, it’s this one, if only because it can absolutely outrun most anyone or anything. You do have to be a little careful because of the speed, or you might find yourself off the highway and in the ocean meeting the Kraken.

According to recent reports, though it may seem like we just had a significant life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

It has been revealed that the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab unveiled today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer stated to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

Sources indicate that starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese Upcoming Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab indicates you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#155130. Tech Report: Upcoming gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1145 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Upcoming gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers in Japan have developed a promising upcoming treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed.
  • Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light.
  • Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers in Japan have developed a promising upcoming treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.

Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.

Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.

The human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play important roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.

One particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.

It has been revealed that treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.

In a recent development, "Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," mentioned Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation.".

Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria.

To overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.

The researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.

Egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.

Sources indicate that the resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.

Industry observers note that to determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.

Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria.

Industry observers note that laboratory experiments revealed that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.

When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.

Recent findings suggest that microscopic examination revealed an vital difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the fresh treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.

The distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.

The researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.

New Treatment Reduces Bone Loss in Mice.

The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.

Recent findings suggest that in mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially important because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.

Industry observers note that analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.

Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.

"Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato stated.

Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.

AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments.

Industry observers note that although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.

To address this challenge, the team plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other key microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.

The researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

Understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.

For now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.

Materials provided by Nagoya University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Before you fly out of the front door and buy up every last 30th anniversary booster pack you can find, these gold cards aren’t available to the public, and there’s no sign as of yet that they ever will be.
  • In a recent development, the 30 Pikachu cards are part of the 999 Gold Card Collection, and they will be on display at the Pokemon Card Art Illustration Exhibition in Shanghai, China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that pokemon released a 30th anniversary TCG expansion in September that was pretty special for several reasons. Chief among them is the 30 special Pikachu cards trainers have been tasked with collecting, and just to make them a little more special, Pokemon has now revealed alternate versions of all 30 cards that have been crafted using pure gold.

Before you fly out of the front door and buy up every last 30th anniversary booster pack you can find, these gold cards aren’t available to the public, and there’s no sign as of yet that they ever will be. The weight of them alone, compared to your average Pokemon card, would make finding them in booster packs and ETBs far too easy.

In a recent development, the 30 Pikachu cards are part of the 999 Gold Card Collection, and they will be on display at the Pokemon Card Art Illustration Exhibition in Shanghai, China. The 999 in the collection’s name comes from the fact that each of the cards is made of 99.9% pure gold. That means each of them weighs about 30g, due to the fact that they’re made out of a precious metal instead of standard gold.

Recent findings suggest that by comparison, a typical Pokemon card weighs about 1.7g, so these special gold cards are about 17 to 18 times heavier than a normal card. As I stated, that would make finding them out in the wild, if they were ever released, incredibly easy. Well, easy if you were lucky enough to happen upon a store selling a booster pack with one of the cards inside, as that pack would be significantly heavier than the rest.

Industry observers note that based on the amount of gold and that gold’s purity, used to make the cards, each one is worth around $3,765. That means there’s almost $113,000 worth of gold in all 30. Ironically, though, if these cards were to ever go on sale, the fact that they’re made of pure gold would almost certainly not be what leads them to fetch an extortionate price at auction.

It has been revealed that these cards are all presumably one of a kind, and it’s that rarity which would really drive up their value. The record for the most expensive Pokemon card ever sold was broken in February of this year when Logan Paul sold his Pikachu Illustrator for $16.492 million, and that doesn’t have a single ounce of gold in it. It’s simply an incredibly rare card in impeccable condition that every TCG collector in the world wishes was a part of their collection.

Recent findings suggest that maybe, like the Pikachu Illustrator that was only ever given to contest winners in the 1990s, some of these pure gold cards will appear in auction houses three decades from now and sell for astronomical amounts we can’t even begin to imagine. For now, just focus on trying to find all 30 of the regular versions, and keep half an eye on 2027, when we’re going to be getting our first-ever three-set expansion to kick off the next Pokemon TCG era after Mega Evolution ends.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old.
  • It has been revealed that "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding fresh content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 enhancement.
  • Recent findings suggest that "The reason for this enhancement is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 update to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are upcoming quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

It has been revealed that "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding fresh content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 enhancement. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

Recent findings suggest that "The reason for this enhancement is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

Sources indicate that as laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

According to recent reports, more clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A fresh opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

According to recent reports, "All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

According to recent reports, you can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a fresh playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

Recent findings suggest that this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

In a recent development, there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

According to recent reports, critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC plans. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

It has been revealed that 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That mentioned, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game presently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

As you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

In a recent development, rounding out the expansion are new enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an update alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

As much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hoYoverse just wrapped up a substantial Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hoYoverse just wrapped up a substantial Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

According to recent reports, much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Sources indicate that version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

Recent findings suggest that general Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other upcoming arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

Sources indicate that when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

In a recent development, version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

It has been revealed that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be unveiled at a later date.

GTA 6: How to Avoid Dye Packs from Marked Bills

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you want to earn massive bucks in GTA 6, you’ll want to rob banks and ATM machines.
  • Industry observers note that picking up marked bills and getting sprayed by dye packs will expose Jason and Lucia and make it easier for cops to notice you.
  • According to recent reports, in order to avoid dye packs and actually claim marked bills, you must first unlock a very important item.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you want to earn massive bucks in GTA 6, you’ll want to rob banks and ATM machines. However, robbing these locations will earn you marked bills, money that has been rigged with dye packs.

Industry observers note that picking up marked bills and getting sprayed by dye packs will expose Jason and Lucia and make it easier for cops to notice you. Additionally, dye packs completely ruin the money you just robbed, meaning you won’t be able to spend it.

According to recent reports, in order to avoid dye packs and actually claim marked bills, you must first unlock a very important item. Read further to learn how to avoid dye packs from marked bills in GTA 6.

In order to avoid getting sprayed by dye packs when picking up marked bills in GTA 6, you must first unlock the Dye Pack Jammer. This valuable item is unlocked in Chapter 3 during the “Credit Check” mission.

Unfortunately, there is no other way to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6, meaning you just have to naturally progress the story until it becomes available. The good news is that it's unmissable.

Sources indicate that credit Check is the 16th mission in Chapter 3, so it’s pretty far along in the game. For reference, it took me about 30 hours to reach this point. Granted, I have been exploring the world thoroughly and completing side objectives, so how long it takes you to reach this mission depends on your playstyle.

During Credit Check, you’ll meet Raul’s group of thieves who are planning a huge bank heist. One of his companions gives you the Dye Pack Jammer to prepare you for the heist.

The Dye Pack Jammer is automatically equipped when you unlock it in Chapter 3. In other words, you don’t have to manually equip it or anything.

Industry observers note that the Dye Pack Jammer allows you to rob any bank in Leonida, as well as towable ATM machines, without worrying that you’ll get sprayed by pink dye. However, the marked bills you earn from these locations aren’t available to use right away.

Industry observers note that in order to turn marked bills into money you can spend, you must bring them to one of the Fence NPCs. Each Fence offers money for marked bills, but Yasmani in Vice City pays the most. You will unlock Yasmani after completing the main story “Boobie Time” in Chapter 3.

If you haven’t claimed the Dye Pack Jammer yet and happened to get covered in dye, then Jason and Lucia will remain exposed to the cops, making exploration and committing robberies much harder. It’s for this reason that you want to remove the dye from your clothes and body as soon as possible.

There are a couple of ways to remove the dye from your characters. First, you can go back to your apartment, take a shower, and change your clothes to remove the dye. Besides that, you can simply wait until it goes away, which takes a long time, or force yourself to get Wasted or Busted.

Industry News: Where To Find The Painted Tunnel In GTA 6

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, driving in GTA 6 is pretty tricky at the best of times and far more realistic than it has ever been in the series before.
  • The prank that multiple players have fallen foul of is a hyper-realistic mural that looks like a tunnel.
  • The idea is that players, especially those in the middle of a police chase, either won’t notice that the through road is actually a painting until it’s too late, or, as many clips have demonstrated, don’t notice it at all and plough headfirst into the mural.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, driving in GTA 6 is pretty tricky at the best of times and far more realistic than it has ever been in the series before. The cops are also harder to shake than ever, which is why the last thing you want when racing away from them at high speed is Rockstar pulling a prank that will bring everything to a grinding halt, literally.

The prank that multiple players have fallen foul of is a hyper-realistic mural that looks like a tunnel. More specifically, it looks like the road you’re on just continues straight ahead, taking you under a bridge.

The idea is that players, especially those in the middle of a police chase, either won’t notice that the through road is actually a painting until it’s too late, or, as many clips have demonstrated, don’t notice it at all and plough headfirst into the mural.

According to recent reports, the more realistic driving in GTA 6 extends beyond how it feels to handle its vehicles. It also applies to what might happen if you were to, say, drive into a wall at 100 mph. Falling for the prank is going to seriously damage your car and cause serious injuries to Jason or Lucia in the process. Maybe even both of them if they’re both in the car.

Industry observers note that the tunnel prank is, naturally, being compared to when the gimmick was used in Looney Tunes cartoons. Most often used by Wile E. Coyote, the iconic cartoon character would often paint tunnels on cliff sides to try and fool Road Runner into trying to use them. Road Runner would usually defy the laws of physics and run right on through. Unfortunately, that’s not possible in GTA 6’s take on the decades-old joke.

Sources indicate that if you want to go and check out the mural yourself, or make a note of where it is in Leonida so you know when to be on high alert, it can be found in the Vice Decor District of Vice City. If you do happen to be on the run and can’t keep an eye on where you are at any given moment, just keep an eye out for a part of the game where murals are popping up on buildings left and right. Odds are you’re in the Decor District, and one of those murals is trying to fool you into crashing headfirst into a solid brick wall.
